text_fidelity_a:
Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold I work in live AV production, and usually keep a pair of Sony over-the-ear headphones in my gear bag for monitoring sound on location. Quality of the sound is important for concert and other live music gigs. But those big Sonys take up a lot of space, so I've been considering a good set of IEMs for a while now. In the past I haven't had good results from anything that wasn't a large over-the-ear set, and I have small ears that reject a lot of ear-bud style devices so I was excited to get a chance to try these out.

Ok, to be fair, I don't have any other IEMs to compare this to, but I'm BLOWN AWAY at how incredible they sound at such a miniscule size. I put on the smallest tips for my ears and they actually stay in relatively well, and create the passive noise cancellation I was expecting but without being uncomfortable to wear for an extended period of time. But the range of sound reproduced was something I have only experienced in larger studio headphones!
A perk of IEMs versus larger headphones on jobs like mine are that I can pull out one so I can hear the sound around me while monitoring with my other ear (great if working with an audio engineer who needs to communicate with me on the job), and it comes with a pretty nifty case to wrap it up and slide into my bag. The case makes it bigger than it needs to be, but honestly this is so much less space than my old headphones took up, and keeps the cord from getting tangled. I love it!
For personal use, they sound great even on consumer equipment, but they really shine on devices that can drive the additional range such as my old LG V20 with it's Quad DAC built in (one of the reasons I keep that old device around!).
The price tag is a little steep for me personally, but my Sony headphones retail somewhere around this (I had bought them used), and I KNOW there are pricier options out there, so it seems to fit right into the audiophile equipment range.
text_fidelity_b: Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold

text_fidelity_a:
Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black I run during the summer and run outside. I hate carrying heavy items with me, like water bottles and phones. I feel they sort of hinder my performance, though I realize it's probably more psychological than physical.
Still, I'm not going to mess with a run I've been accustomed to for nearly twenty years, but I do wish, more often than not, that I had some way of tracking my run and how many miles I've done *exactly* while being outside. Sure, I can track the mileage by checking my phone before and after, but it would be nice to have a tracker on me without adding any psychological weight. I used to have a Polar watch that worked fine, but it died some time ago and I never bothered to get a replacement.
But finally I did.

With this one, I'm able to wear the watch without toting my phone along and it still carries all the features and tracking as if the phone were connected to any other tracking watch. While this watch is used for a number of cardio activities, I use it only for running. There are "pages" of exercises you can track, but for a quick run the default is set on the bottom left button--very nice to have, especially for me. Not sure if you can change the default on there to another exercise, but for me it's perfect and I haven't bothered looking up how to change it.
But curious to check out the full features, I ventured into the different pages (or screens) the watch has to offer. During my course, I found that the buttons were *very* stiff. This might be to prevent accidental presses during exercise, but I found that I had to press almost twice has hard as other electronic watches for the watch to recognize my press. But, from my uses so far, I've pressed it mostly to view all the screens when testing out all the features. When actually running, I do no more than a few presses before and after each run. The network had trouble activating itself in the beginning, but that's because I was fiddling with it outside. It kept trying to set itself numerous times when I actually ran outside, but I always dismissed it. Once, however, I was under the open sky I let it connect and it has had no problem or delay connecting ever since.

After every run I am able to sync it with the Epson app, as well as RunKeeper. People have complained about the Epson app but I find it neat and useful.

Overall, it's a great little watch that accurately records my runs and uploads them without the use of the phone during the workout. I'm able to review it speedily on my phone right after, and I love that I can now track my progress without the burden of added weight. It's pricey for sure, but considering I don't need my phone and my previous watch lasted me ten years, I'm sure this watch will be a great investment that will last me hopefully for another decade or so.
text_fidelity_b: Epson E11E223052 ProSense 367 GPS Multisport Watch with Ultra Long Battery Life and Sapphire Glass - Black

text_fidelity_a:
MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.
* Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc.
* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!

My title for this review is not deliberately obtuse, it is just that I was desperate for an antenna and chose the one with the reviews that seemed to best meet my housing needs (apartment) as well as my budgetary needs (retired with small, fixed income).

You know, these small antenna types can only provide as well as they can, given their limited powers and whatever physical/geographic challenges are caused by one's limits on where the thing can be placed.

I do not live surrounded by mountains or trees or large buildings. I do not live in a valley or in the middle of nowhere. I DO live within forty miles of every transmission source in a nearby big city, so it might be considered reasonable to expect that an antenna that touts a sixty-mile range to be useful.

It is, but only partially because the fault is not in our stars, it is in a huge menu of influences (which may include the some sky/heavenly/ astronomical stuff, but that is another story).

My point, and the useful part, is that these simple and, more importantly, cheap antennas can only do what they can because geography, distance, obstacles you cannot see or image and even the stars (yep) conspire to modify their successful use, and even all that can be affected by other stuff we are unable to anticipate or influence.

If you want an antenna that has a potential for reasonable performance, simply spend the considerable dollars that will buy a reasonably and consistent performance.

Sellers, provide honest claims so that purchasers will know what they are getting. Customers, be discerning so that you can use your dollars to get the best you and your critical thinking can provide.

As for me, hope springs eternal that I will someday be able afford an antenna that allows me to watch our local PBS stations and in the meantime I will ignore the religious (not aligned with my personal spiritual practices) and selling-stuff channels.

It is the best I can afford, and a little late-night cartoons never hurt anyone.

The four-star rating is only because I finally hold a decent perspective on all this jazz.

I was using this to briefly control two systems with a single mouse/keyboard, and it did work for this purpose. I could easily control both of them. However, I found that the hub would occasionally, without apparent cause, reset itself, causing the mouse and keyboard to be re-detected, flickering the keyboard backlight and triggering the beeps and chimes of the OS detected a connected device. Same occurred in two different power outlets, and multiple USB ports. It wasn't a major issue - everything was always redetected and working again within seconds, without my needing to do anything, but it was mildly annoying.

It is possible that it was one of my computers - the reason I was using it was that I was transitioning over to a new computer due to various issues, after all. Maybe the USB controller wasn't outputting a clean, consistent signal.

If you need this temporarily while transitioning over to a new system, or in a system which is isn't used that much, it should be fine. I wouldn't use it as a interface for my primary setup though.

text_fidelity_a: BenQ EW277HDR Eye Care 27 inch 1080p Monitor | Optimized for Home & Office with Adaptive Brightness Technology Maybe it is just because I haven't upgraded my monitor in a long time and maybe it is because this is the biggest monitor I have ever had on a computer, but I love this monitor.  Since I spend a lot of time on the computer, this has a feature that is very important to me, which is low blue light emissions.  The blue light that comes from monitors is not good for our eyes, so a monitor that claims to reduce that is a good thing, if it really works.  I don't know how to tell for sure, but after using the monitor for several days, it does seem that I suffer less eye fatigue.  The monitor also has a "bright intelligence" button that automatically dims or brightens the screen depending on light levels, which helps reduce eye fatigue.  This feature can be turned on or off to your preference.  There a number of different light adjustments on the monitor and they are not difficult to select, once you figure out the buttons to set them.  There are 5 adjustment buttons, but none are assigned to a specific function, but there is a way to assign some of the buttons, so they are configurable to some extent.  Initially, you press any one of the buttons to bring up a five selection menu on screen that allows you to adjust brightness, depending on what you are doing (web surfing, multimedia, office or reading) as well contrast and sharpness.  There are various other display adjustments for positioning the screen (which I had to use, since the screen was initially slightly off center at the highest resolution).  Also there are adjustments buttons for sound, if you use the built-in speakers and for auto shutoff time (choice of OFF, 10, 20 and 30 minutes).  There are various other settings.  I don't quite understand all the settings, but there is an included manual on the CD that comes with the monitor and the manual seems very complete, is well written and easy to understand.  My monitor also included an HDMI cable.  I tried using HDMI, but couldn't see much difference in that and the older type of connector (which they call D-Sub, also known as VGA, which is an analog connection vs. digital).  If you are watching Blu-Ray movies, HDMI should give you a better picture.  I don't have any Blu-Ray movies, nor a DVD drive that supports Blu-Ray, so no need for HDMI.  Also, I use a KVM switch to control several computers and that doesn't support HDMI connectors.  The included CD also has any drivers you might need, but the monitor worked perfectly on Windows 10 without the need to install any drivers.  The HDMI connection did bring sound to the built-in speakers, as well as the picture, but the sound volume was extremely low, even at 100%.  When I used the other connector (D-Sub), and a separate audio cable, the sound volume was much better.  Maybe something I am setting incorrectly?  Also, typical of speakers built-in to a monitor, the sound quality is very poor.  If you listen to music much at all, you will want to stick with external speakers.  This is probably typical of all monitors with built-in speakers.  It was disappointing, but not unexpected.  The monitor is very lightweight, so it is very easy to move.  Has a nice low profile base.  Can be tipped to a desirable viewing angle, but no height adjustment.  There is a lot to this monitor and to take full advantage of it, I will need to read the manual to understand all the available settings.  Requires a 2 step assembly of the base, but it is very easy; you should be up and running in mere minutes.  This can be wall mounted, but requires a separate wall mount kit, which is not included.  Overall, a great monitor that should meet the needs of just about anyone.  With a 3-year warranty, you can't go wrong.
text_fidelity_b: BenQ EW277HDR Eye Care 27 inch 1080p Monitor | Optimized for Home & Office with Adaptive Brightness Technology

text_fidelity_a:
ibi - The Smart Photo Manager - Collect, Organize and Privately Share Photos & Videos from Smartphones, Cloud and Social Media Accounts - US Version IBI - THE SMART PHOTO MANAGER (US Version) makes it super easy to extract, back up, and share photos stored on my mobile devices. Instead of emailing cell phone photos that I want to share among electronic devices (an iPad Air (3rd Gen), a desktop PC, and a Samsung Galaxy cell phone), I can upload the photos to Ibi via a network connection with only a couple of clicks in the Ibi app.

No longer do I have to address an email, select and add the photos, send the email--and then reverse the process on a second device (open the email, download the photos, and save the photos to the device). All that’s necessary is to take the photos, open the Ibi app, choose “import photos”, select the photos, and hit the import button.

The photos are immediately uploaded to Ibi, and I can access them immediately on all of my other devices. There is no need to clutter up email or to consume precious storage space on my mobile devices, when all I want to do is share photos.

Ibi is extremely versatile. It allows you to sort and organize photos, and create Albums. It allows you to authorize certain people to email photos directly to Ibi. It allows you to set up different areas of Ibi for the use of individuals. It allows you to upload its contents to a PC or other even larger storage device by plugging in a USB cable (not included). It even allows you to stream your videos to a television set (using Chromecast or Roku apps).

Ibi is easy to set up, using Bluetooth. My iPad and my Galaxy phone both found the powered on (plugged in) Ibi in less than 30 seconds. Once set up, Ibi communicates via your home network’s Internet access. When your Ibi app is set up, click on Help, and download the complete user manual (a PDF file). The manual is easy to understand, and will enable you to get the most out of your Ibi.

Ibi is a small drive that easily fits on a bookshelf. It uses just one power cord. I really love this Ibi storage drive. It is simplifying my life.

+++++IMPORTANT NOTE: You should NOT choose “automatic backup” in the Ibi app Settings until you understand how the app works. With automatic backup enabled, Ibi will copy all of the photos stored on EACH mobile device, and you will probably get a lot of duplicate photos. For example, if you have been sharing and storing the same photos on an iPad and a cell phone, Ibi will copy the photos from each device. Worse, if you go into Ibi and delete the duplicates, Ibi will keep automatically adding the photos back as long as the photos still exist in storage on the two different devices.

You will probably want to use “automatic backup” when you first set up your Ibi. That way all of your photos will be automatically copied to Ibi to start you off. But you should turn “automatic backup” off before you start deleting duplicate photos. You will never have a problem with duplicate photos if automatic backup is turned off.+++++
text_fidelity_b: ibi - The Smart Photo Manager - Collect, Organize and Privately Share Photos & Videos from Smartphones, Cloud and Social Media Accounts - US Version

text_fidelity_a: WD 8TB My Book Desktop External Hard Drive, USB 3.0, External HDD with Password Protection and Backup Software - WDBBGB0080HBK-NESN Buyers should note that this drive is formatted in exFAT. Without knowing this, I plugged it in to a running computer and began to transfer some files. The computer was shut down for the night. The next morning, I found that the computer refused to boot up with the new drive installed. Unplugged the drive, and the computer booted up fine. Finally checked the file system. Found it to be exFAT. Moved the files off and re-formatted the drive to NTFS and the problem went away. I suggest anyone purchasing this unit just save yourself the time and trouble and reformat it right out of the box. The software on the drive isn't needed anyway. I have several Western Digital external drives and this is the first one that arrived in a format other than NTFS.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I prefer trackballs to mice and I have been looking for a good wireless trackball as my primary system is a laptop. In the past I had a Logitech TrackMan II, a hideous device that made my hands hurt. Logitech's new M570 trackball is far and away better than that TrackMan II, and I would consider it an excellent device except for one thing.

I have large hands, and as a consequence I need larger pointing devices to fit my hand. The M570 is marginally larger than my standard mouse which gave me pause right off the bat, but my concerns were unfounded. Even though this trackball device is not especially large, it fits my hand comfortably and I can spin the ball with ease without cramping my hands. My finger tips rest on the buttons and my thumb tip rests on the ball, while the fleshy part of my palm is on the desk past the plastic base. Finally, a trackball that fits my hand much like a normal mouse.

I have a marble mouse and while it's a decent trackball-like device, the ball easily drops out when the device is inverted and as a result I have dropped the ball one too many times and chipped it. The M570 holds the ball in place and does not allow it to simply come out without applying deliberate pressure, resulting in less opportunities to either lose or damage the ball.

The ball itself is a pretty shade of blue and, with the exception of the finger holes, looks a lot like a miniature bowling ball.

The M570 has 4 buttons and a scroll wheel that can be pressed for a total of 5 programmable buttons. The one problem with this trackball involves the scroll wheel - there is no horizontal scroll. While this is really just an inconvenience, horizontal scrolling has become very commonplace and that it is not included is a disappointment.

The range on the M570 us excellent. I am able to control the pointer on the screen from a distance of 15' - 20' away without any issues at all (except that it's harder to read the screen). This is very convenient and will be immeasurably helpful for presentations where the desk is a good distance from the computer and control is needed across that distance.

I am very pleased with the Logitech M570 wireless trackball and can heartily recommend it. The one improvement would be horizontal scrolling; otherwise, this trackball is superb.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red If you have a Thunderbolt 3-equipped computer, this drive provides speeds approaching the highest-end built-in SSDs. Case in point: I have a 2018 MacBook Pro with top specs. Its internal SSD is a screamer. And, as you can see from my screen shots, the X5 is right in the same neighborhood. These tests were run on my computer while it was running a bunch of other things (Word, Excel, VMWare Fusion, Mail.app, Safari with about 15 tabs open), so it represents real-world use.

And, as you can see, the X5 is really fast. If you need speed and have Thunderbolt 3, this is a great drive.

Installation was easy. My Mac recognized the drive right away. I could've just used it, but Samsung provides a utility on the drive for enabling its onboard encryption and keeping its firmware up to data. Recommended.

(But do make sure your computer has Thunderbolt 3. You can't tell just by looking at the ports, as TB3 is implemented as a superset of USB-C. So, Thunderbolt 3 is USB-C but the converse is not true. Similarly, previous-rev Thunderbolt interfaces aren't forward-compatible to TB3 devices. Some of the one-star reviews of this drive are clearly from folks who didn't know these issues.)
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG X5 Portable SSD - 2TB - Thunderbolt 3 External SSD (MU-PB2T0B/AM) Gray/Red

Portable Sound Bar for TV/PC, 105dB Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless & Wired Soundbar with 2200 mAh Battery, 3D Surround Sound Home Theater Built-in Subwoofer with Remote Control for Projectors/Phones/Tablets As a layman mom buying this for my teen son I wasn’t sure what exactly I was looking for.. except, my teen asked me for sound!! So, knowing this just had to suffice… I came across the sound bar and following recommendations from others- I took a chance and I’m so glad I did. One needs to know.. for the price point this exceeds all expectations!! I do believe we need to keep expectations within reason… Not said as an excuse but, for what you’re paying and getting the two are sound deal. This isn’t going to sound like a Blau punk deluxe stereo- But, if a quality upgrade is what you’re after.. Check this out !!! Also, don’t be intimidated by the electronic aspect- IF, I can set this up.. I promise anyone can! (trust me, I can barely change remote control from TV to DVR- and I did this step-by-step!!)

Perks:

•easy set up and includes all wires and connectors you’ll need. No extra purchase needed. (however, you must have a wall butt for usb cord to plug into socket.)

•instructions are straight forward and easy to follow. We connected to a TV and PS4 station combo.. step-by-step “how to” worked on the first try and that never happens!

•genuine quality and impresses those who’ve played on the game box since.. my son is feeling pretty cool about now- it’s a “sub-woofer” for his game.. ha ha!!!

•comes with a controller so, the convenience it’s all there for the user.

•at a price point of $40- this performs at a much higher quality.. I would never have thought the entire speaker, adapters and remote would be found at such a steal of a deal... and perform so well!!

Quirks:
•this only connects to wall with USB cord. There is no standard plug attached. Note: you will need to provide your own “wall butt..” and I’m assuming we all have one with our cell phones?! But, be sure to have an extra wall butt/socket plug handy for inserting the USB cord and connecting it to the wall.

•position of the remote eye is dead center in middle of the bar.. So, be careful not to block it with TV or, furniture lip.. or, anything else! Otherwise, the sound bar remote cannot connect.

•the actual USB cord is far to short for our outlet.. and may also be for most? this caused angst to reach the outlet. So, we had to swap the cord with another we had in the house that was longer.. it would be nice if longer cord came standard- this would be my biggest complaint with this.. and that is it.

Overall- this is A lot of bang for your buck! It will make a solid difference and not break the bank.. it is easy, straightforward connecting- One I can recommend without hesitation! I hope this info can help your decision… Feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: Portable Sound Bar for TV/PC, 105dB Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless & Wired Soundbar with 2200 mAh Battery, 3D Surround Sound Home Theater Built-in Subwoofer with Remote Control for Projectors/Phones/Tablets

I ordered this Cooling Pad for my very heavy and large 17" Gaming laptop which I am mainly using for video and photo editing. Though this Klim Ultimate is made of plastic, it handles the larger laptop just fine. This cooling pad has a USB cable that plugs into your laptop for power. I was worried that it was not going to work as the cable splits into two USB plugs and my laptop only has one USB plug on either side of the laptop so the cable will not allow for both USB plugs to plug into the laptop. When one side is plugged in, the other USB plug will not reach to the other side of the laptop. The cooling pad does however work if only one USB plug is plugged into the laptop for both the fan and RGB lights. I am not really sure yet if I were to use a USB dock, and plug both cables into that, if the speed of the fan would be faster but I doubt it. For my use it seems to work fine and although the Cooling pad has a speed control dial, I only use it on the highest setting and the noise level really isn't that bad. Overall for the money, I feel that this is actually a really great value and the RGB lighting is a fun bonus.

Just plug the transmitter in near you router and plug the Ethernet cable into an open port. Plug the receiver where you need the signal press the button on each device and setup is about complete. I had zero issues in terms of connection.

The farther the distance you span and the more walls and obstacles between, the slower the resultant signal will be. I tested the unit in a multitude of locations and I always received a signal, although it dropped the farther away I moved.

The point of this device is to use in locations where it is not possible, or where it would be difficult to run an Ethernet cable. If you are in a position where you need to get a signal to a TV to stream programming this would be a great choice. I tested it with Hulu, Prime and Netflix and it worked great. Depending on distance spanned and the strength of your original signal it probably would be adequate for internet use. However I can not recommend this as a viable option for gaming.

This set will definitely fulfill many people’s needs. It is just important to consider your use in relation to the WiFi product you install. For my family this worked fairly well.

text_fidelity_a:
Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa I'm not a gamer, but I do have around 30 devices connected to a home network. These include WEMO switches, Amazon Echos, a smart TV, a playstation, Kindles, iPads, printers, and smartphones. The "dynamic Quality of Service" feature of this NIGHTHAWK X4 ULTIMATE GAMING ROUTER (R7500v2) seems to prioritize these devices, so that all of them are more responsive (faster connections) than they were with my previous router (a rock-solid NIGHTHAWK (R7000)).

When this NIGHTHAWK (R7500v2) is set up, it recognizes all of the "Internet of things" devices for what they are. In the "attached devices" list, these aren't given device names (e.g., "iPad", picked up from the device itself) but have "n/a" in the name column (and you can't assign them names even if you know them by the MAC numbers). I don't know exactly how the "Quality of Service" feature performs its magic, but now when I ask an Amazon Echo to turn on a light or a fan, the Echo performs the task immediately--instead of with a delay while it searched through the router's list of connected devices for the correct one.

The PCs and other devices that use lots of bandwidth (instead of being on standby much of the time) seem to connect faster, and they test (using OOKLA) at significantly faster Internet speeds.

My R7500v2 is broadcasting signals for both bands (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz), and my compatible devices connect with the 5 GHz network whenever I ask them to. However, I don't use the 5 GHz band for anything at present (because it's easiest to have everything that uses a printer on the same band with the printers). Thus I don't know whether the router frequently drops the 5 GHz signal, as other reviewers have stated.

I've used several high-end Linksys routers, and they have performed very well. However, I find that Netgear routers lose their Internet signal far less often, and almost never require rebooting--when Netgear routers need rebooting, the issue is almost always traceable to Comcast problems.

Another reason that I prefer Netgear routers over Linksys routers is that Netgear has no limit (or a very high limit) on the number of devices that you can list by MAC number and tell the router to "allow only these devices to connect to the network". I use this feature as an extra firewall, and find that the Linksys 25-device list is inadequate for my needs.

Finally, the Netgear "Genie" app for managing the router settings is clear and easy to understand. The initial setup for this router is easy, unless you have a nonstandard home network (e.g., my router is connected with the Comcast-supplied equipment in "Bridge" mode), and/or you interrupt the setup routine before it's run through all its steps. If you do land in setup limbo, you can start over by resetting the router to the factory settings (use a paperclip to hold down the reset button for 10-30 seconds--light will blink; unplug from wall for 30 seconds; follow Quick Start instructions again from beginning).
text_fidelity_b: Netgear R7500-200NAS Nighthawk X4 Ultimate Gaming Router - AC2350 4X4 MU-MIMO Dual Band WiFi Gigabit Router (R7500v2) with Open Source Support. Compatible with Amazon Echo/Alexa

Samson LTS50 Laptop Stand (SALTS50), Packs, Black I purchased this to support a [[ASIN:B00ND1KHY2 Mackie Mix Series Mix12FX -Watt 12-Channel Mixer]], which it easily does. What impressed me the most is the construction. I had been using a music stand with the tray perpendicular to the ground and it worked, but was not nearly as stable as this stand. Moreover, I looked at a few other brands, but most were cheaply made.

Here are a few things that set this one apart: first, the clamping mechanisms are quick release type and not the cheesy knobs that every other stand I tried employs. Second, if you are considering this for a truly heavy device like a projector the pins for the support pole guarantee that it will be supported. Frankly, the pins are probably never going to be needed because the main release mechanisms hold firmly.

Dimensions are:
Tray: 15 9/16 x 10 7/8 inches with lips along the widths top and bottom.
Stand: adjusts from 23 to 53 inches - this is ideal if you are a keyboardist or drummer who wants to control your instrument and mics via a mixer because the height range is perfect for most scenarios.
Footprint: 25 inches between tripod feet points.

This also comes with a sticky silicone pad that measures 12 x 7 5/78 inches to hold a mixer or laptop firmly in place. My Mackie mixer did not budge when it was placed on the pad and the table tilted 30 degrees.

Finally, I purchased a [[ASIN:B000XZYXTG Hamilton Carrying Bag for KB50 & KB990 Series Stands]] that easily holds and protects this stand. I recommend it if you do opt for this model.

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic HomeHawk Window Home Monitoring Camera for Outdoor Monitoring, Mounts to Inside Window, Color Night Vision, Wide Angle, 24/7 Full HD Recording, Person Detection, Alexa Compatible KX-HNC500 I've used cheap Wyze cameras as well as more expensive cameras like Arlo in my garage, but wi-fi is pretty iffy there. I wanted to see if the wi-fi receiver in this HomeHawk beats the Wyze or Arlo, but unfortunately, that's not the case. The HomeHawk struggled in my garage as much as the others did. As a matter of fact, I couldn't connect to it at all. So right off the bat, that is something to note... that paying more for a camera doesn't necessarily mean better wi-fi receivers are inside the camera. This isn't something I'm going to subtract a star for since no cameras on the market can help with my wi-fi situation, that's something that will have to be remedied by wi-fi extenders.

Now once I move this camera indoor, with better wi-fi reception, to monitor the backyard, it does the job wonderfully! The app is great and full of features. Be sure you select the proper MODE. By default, it was on BASIC and it did not do any recordings. I realize I had to change it to PROTECTION mode or 24/7 mode. Or, better yet, you can create your own mode! You can determine if it will record 24/7, or only when it detects motion. You can determine the duration of the clip. Now that is pretty cool! The default is 10 seconds, and for several weeks I thought I had to live with the default, until I discovered that I can actually change this by creating my own Mode. You can determine if it will notify you for every motion detected, or only for human detections. Lastly, you can name the mode anything you want, then select it and you're set! I've only used Wyze, Arlo and Homehawk cameras, and without a doubt, this Panasonic software is the best of the bunch. 5-stars!
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic HomeHawk Window Home Monitoring Camera for Outdoor Monitoring, Mounts to Inside Window, Color Night Vision, Wide Angle, 24/7 Full HD Recording, Person Detection, Alexa Compatible KX-HNC500

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers Our daughters' charter school uses Kindle readers for their textbooks so we bought them each one Sept. 2011. Both Kindles are still working really well, and we're pleased with their durability. Because of the daily use during the week, they need to charge them every couple of days. But that is a simple matter to take care of. Once they've finished their homework they plug them in, then in the morning unplug before we head off for school. I have noticed that due to the frequent use, the numbers & letters have worn off of most of the keys. That could be a bit of an issue but the girls have memorized which key is for which letter or number.

I like how there's little to no glare in the sun, the Kindle is easier to read than other readers or a tablet. Because of the ease in obtaining books, especially many of the Classics for free, the Kindle has increased our daughters' love of reading even more. My one small complaint with the charger is that the white plastic cover on the cord is splitting near the end pieces. I've considered contacting Amazon regarding that because it's obvious that it's due to a defect. If I do, I'll update here.

Overall, we're very happy with Kindle and plan at some point to buy more readers for the rest of the family.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Z623 400 Watt Home Speaker System, 2.1 Speaker System - Black Latest edit after some frustrating months of use.

I ordered this as a TV speaker. That was in the description.
With no remote, and no way to raise or lower the sound without getting up, the item is useless to me. I like to watch TV in bed.
Who wants to keep getting up. As a computer speaker, it takes up a lot of space.very dissapointed.
I will donate it a church, where they will appreciate a loud speaker for youth groups.

Edit after 5 days use.

There is no remote. The volume is controlled by a dial. When using this connected to your TV, it's a major disadvantage getting up every time you need to change the volume. I have to downgrade from 5 stars to 4, because of this. They need to add to either a remote, or an app letting your phone control the volume. Not a problem when using this as a computer speaker, since the control is by your hand, not across the room. This is promoted as a TV speaker, not just a computer speaker, so it's a major fault.

Original review below.

I have been using the Logitech Z2300 that I purchased years ago. Connected to my computer and much appreciated when I listen to my apple subscription music. A real monster for a computer speaker. Thankfully, the Z 625 is decidedly smaller and fits on the bottom shelf of my 42 inch wood TV table with room to spare. There is also room left for my Amazon Echo and Braven wireless bluetooth speakers. The smaller size results in a much cleaner, more attractive package.

The dialog is much clearer than I expected. I have a ZVOX 450 on my main TV, so I do appreciate clear dialog.
I was disappointed that there is no bluetooth. The computer and Man Cave TV are on opposite sides of the same room, and having the Z2300 for music, and the Z625 for the TV is a bit too much. However, the problem was easily solved. On the Z625, I'm using the optical cable for the TV sound, and am using the enclosed jack to connect the speaker to my extra Iphone. As I type, I'm listening to Herman's Hermits through my Iphone to Z625 jack connection. The music is very soothing and suits my needs perfectly. No adjustments are needed when switching from the music through my smartphone via jack, or the TV sound through the optical cable. Automatic switching,

My TV test via optical was the opening of Game of Thrones. The subwoofer bass sounded great and added greatly to the enjoyment of watching the series. The galloping horses sounded thunderous.

Other considerations. I gave away my monstrous Polk system when we moved to our condo. Soundbars provide the cleanest look but really don't have any bass. My wife is picky. The soundbar is on the main TV for a cleaner appearance, while the Man Cave is a perfect home for this unit.

There was absolutely no documentation/instructions in the box, other than safety information. However hookup instructions were printed on the cardboard box. Don't destroy them opening it. Hooking up via optical was very intuitive and took minutes. I'd still like some instructions. For example, the power button is a push button. Does it shut off after inactivity? I'm doing it manually. Going by the Z2300, it probably won't make any difference. These are built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Z623 400 Watt Home Speaker System, 2.1 Speaker System - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Meta Portal - Smart Video Calling for the Home with 10” Touch Screen Display - White We've been using an older first generation Portal and like it very much. I was not expecting to be so impressed with this one, but wow have they managed to improve almost everything about the original! It still has the very cool zoom-and-pan style camera feature that follows the subject, as well as all the fun filters and of course my kids' favorite, story time... but the polish and style of this unit is really premium. The speaker is fantastic and LOUD if you want it to be. The clarity and bass rivals my bookshelf speakers so well, sometimes the kids play music off it and I could have sworn they were using the speakers in the living room. But the biggest improvement over the previous generation is the ability to run off battery power and move around. The "portable portal" honestly makes so much sense, I wonder why the original stationary style ones came out first!
Make no mistake, it is NOT a tablet, it is not thin and won't fit in an attaché case nicely. It is wedge-shaped making it stand easily at an ideal angle, and even has a cut-out handle to pick it up and carry it to a better location for video chat. This is great for bringing it to wherever my kids happen to be congregating currently, and it can be put back up on the shelf when done to charge. Like the original Portals, it has Alexa built in and can act as an Echo for most things, however it is very tied into Facebook's ecosystem. That means that although it seems to run something akin to Android behind the scenes, this is NOT going to offer a standard App store, and even things like Youtube are not available for it (licensing issues with Google I'd suppose). However there is a browser, and you can navigate to YouTube and play it from the website just fine, although a proper app would be much easier to navigate. It does have Plex support, which I found interesting since I have a Plex server. I never thought I'd find Plex available where Youtube is not! Meanwhile, between Youtube in the browser, Amazon Music through Alexa and content on Plex, there are plenty of ways to make it a music streamer on that glorious better-than-it-should-sound speaker. And the camera works just as well if not better than the OG Portal!

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Wireless N300 Mbps Extreme-N Gigabit Router (DIR-655) We are very satisfied with the two DIR-655s that we have (at two sites). They hold up well and cause no problems. They're fast and stable; they run cool and basically require little or no attention.

Two router features that deserve much more discussion than they usually get are the unit's firewall (if any) and its Quality-of-Service (QoS) engine (if any).

o The firewall keeps external probes and hack-attempts out of your network. You'd be amazed how many probes a home or business broadband connection gets every hour from places like China, Eastern Europe and the Middle East. They're looking for ways in so they can infect your machines and steal your information. A router with a good firewall implemented in its firmware is increasingly essential. Firewalls let internal users establish connections with remote machines, not the other way around. And the DIR-655's firewall is excellent, a stateful-packet-inspection implementation that is truly industrial-class. Frankly, I didn't know this when I bought my first unit but was delighted to discover it once I brought it home. Good stuff. And, it's compatible with my company's virtual-private-network (VPN) approaches, which can be a real problem for firewalls to accommodate. My company has used two VPN approaches in the time I've had our DIR-655s, and there have been no issues.

o A good QoS engine prioritizes time-critical Internet traffic such as voice-over-Internet (VoIP). I did not fully appreciate this until we pulled the plug on our landline and implemented "roll-your-own VoIP", saving 90% off our monthly phone costs (see [...] for details). Only a router with good QoS capabilities will allow phone calls to be clear, crisp and smooth in the face of other Internet traffic. And the DIR-655 turns out to have a very good QoS engine. It automatically prioritizes the standard VoIP ports so our phone calls sound as good as a landline even with two teenagers streaming video, cruising Facebook, listening to Pandora, Skyping and FaceTime-ing, etc. Unfortunately, the marketplace is not yet fully aware of the benefits of a good QoS engine in routers, so it's not a given. Even Apple's well-regarded and excellent Time Capsule and Airport/Airport Extreme routers don't have it, for example. But DIR-655 does.

The only issue we've ever experienced with the DIR-655s in our years of usage was once when a cell phone got into a conniption loop that had it disassociate and reassociate with the router over and over and over again, many times per minute. This caused the router to bog down and reboot itself (and who could blame it). The DIR-655's informative logs helped me diagnose what was going on. Eventually the phone got straightened out, and the problem went away.

UPDATE: I can no longer recommend this router. The latest firmware is abysmal and ruins what was formerly a good product.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wireless N300 Mbps Extreme-N Gigabit Router (DIR-655)

text_fidelity_a:
TREBLAB Z2 | Over Ear Workout Headphones with Microphone | Bluetooth 5.0, Active Noise Cancelling (ANC) | Up to 35H Battery Life | Wireless Headphones for Sport, Workout, Running, Gym I wanted to find a cheaper alternative to my wife's wireless Bose headset, something with decent noise cancelling for flights and work. So far I've used Bose, the MPOW H5, Treblab, and Woltix with ANC.

The sound on these are first class - really great highs, mids, and lows - tons of clarity (when active noise cancel is on...otherwise it sounds a bit muggy). Very comfortable and light. BUT - I got these because they are wireless with active noise cancellation, and although the ANC is effective, if you are in a quiet room you'll hear a slight hiss when the ANC is on - many people report the same thing in reviews, and it's true - you'll hear it. You won't notice this when music is on or during a flight. I often use these at coffee shops just to zone out and focus on work, and I could notice the slight hiss in quieter environments.

I've also used Bose, the MPOW H5, and Woltix with ANC. I didn't want to buy another Bose headset when my wife and I travel together. Nothing will compare to Bose noise cancellation, but the MPOW H5 and Woltix are actually really nice for the money. The MPOW H5 don't have as good audio clarity as the Treblab, but at the end of the day I got noise cancelling headphones for the noise canceling. I ended up returning the Treblab and the MPOW H5 and I kept the Woltix because they are more comfortable than the MPOW and had the best low-price ANC. The MPOW also had some sound interference issues randomly when the ANC was on.

So:

Bose: Best noise cancellation, good audio, comfortable, but definitely expensive!
Treblab: Best audio, worst noise cancellation (you can hear a slight hiss when turned on), comfortable, but large and they don't fold down too small.
MPOW: Good audio, good noise cancellation, but was getting some weird sound interference with the ANC on sometimes. Tight on ears.
Woltix: Good audio, good noise cancellation, most comfortable (way lighter and less tight on the ears than the MPOW), and fold down the smallest.
text_fidelity_b: TREBLAB Z2 | Over Ear Workout Headphones with Microphone | Bluetooth 5.0, Active Noise Cancelling (ANC) | Up to 35H Battery Life | Wireless Headphones for Sport, Workout, Running, Gym

text_fidelity_a:
DeLorme Earthmate PN-40 Waterproof Hiking GPS I purchased a Delorme PN-40 GPS for the purpose of geocaching. I already own a Garmin GPSMap 60CSx and a Garmin eTrex Legend, so although I did not really need another unit I wanted one so that when geocaching with my kids we would each be carrying a GPS and not reliant on one another. I have been very satisfied with my Garmin units but was impressed with the reviews and feature set of the Delorme, so I bought it with the expectation of it being acceptable for my uses as a backup unit. It has exceeded my expectations. It is not without flaws but it is a tremendous GPS that is very much worth every penny of the purchase price.

It is very similar in hard interface layout to my 60CSx, with the same buttons doing similar functions though in different locations. This makes working with the Delorme simple in that I immediately found myself familiar with how to work this GPS. The software interface is different, though, and is unlike any other unit with which I have worked. Different is not wrong, but it means a learning curve for those who use Garmin or Magellan units.

The first power-on of this unit is the most painful as it searches for the satellites. After this initial acquisition, however, power-up is always appreciably faster and the acquisition of satellites faster.

Once the GPS has acquired the satellites, it has proven itself to be very accurate and stable. It is not unusual to navigate to a location and have the unit lead me to a point less than a foot away from the lat/long specified. Reported accuracy on the screen is typically between 6 and 11 feet.

The accuracy does diminish under heavy canopy but no more so than my Garmins do. In dense tree cover I found that it maintains its location quite well most of the time, though it occasionally gets confused and leads me in circles. It seems to do this at times when my 60CSx is having no trouble, but it also seems to have no trouble when the Garmins are confused. This brings up a good point - different GPS manufacturers, using differing chip sets, will have varying environments in which their GPS units work better than others and sometimes not as well as others. It is important to keep this in mind and to select a unit that is best suited for the need.

The compass is excellent. Once calibrated it seems to be very accurate and does not need for the unit to be held level flat when in use in order to get a correct bearing. The 3D compass is something that is lacking in my Garmin units, but newer units have this feature now and it's wonderful. Manually calibrating the compass is easy and all you have to do is to follow the instructions on the screen (it equates to a series of arm motions).

This is a rugged and sturdy unit and can handle some jostling. It does as well in wet, rainy weather as it does on clear days. It is waterproof and can be submerged, but I am not daring enough to try this voluntarily.

One point on which many people complain is the screen size. Yes, it has a smaller screen than average units but it also seems to be bright and readable even in direct sunlight. Sure, larger would be nice but clear and readable is far preferable.

Delorme ships their Topo product with this GPS and it is the deal-maker that gives this GPS a decided edge. The maps may be cut and transferred to the PN-40 through Topo, or the pre-cut maps may be used instead. To get Garmin's MapSource costs an extra $100, which makes the PN-40 an even better deal. The maps are of good quality and are sufficient for hiking and driving alike. For most uses the pre-cup maps will be sufficient, but higher resolution images can be cut from Topo.

Right out of the box, my PN-40 was defective and had problem with the screen. I was not convinced that it was a problem until I called Delorme, and I was told to ship it back. In one week's time I had a completely new unit that has worked flawlessly ever since. While I was disappointed with the first unit being defective, I was shocked at how responsive Delorme is to customer requests for assistance. It is clear to me that they stand behind their product.

Less than three weeks after I purchased my PN-40, Delorme released Topo 8. My unit shipped with Topo 7. I called Delorme and asked about an upgrade, and for the cost of shipping a new Topo 8 DVD set was sent to me.

Map updates on the PN-40 are FAST. Scrolling is not exactly smooth but the dual-core processor embedded within keeps up quite admirably.

One drawback with this unit is that, at this time, importing waypoints and geocaches requires a different software set than can be used with Garmin and Magellan units. It can be done with Topo, and for geocachers there is Cache Register, but GSAK and other common tools do not transfer successfully at this time. Hopefully this will be remedied in the near future. Granted, this is easy enough to do, but one cannot have a single software application that can work with multiple units of different brand.

Another drawback is that this GPS loves batteries. On new, fully-charged NiMH batteries one can expect maybe 10 hours of operation before the unit gracefully turns itself off. On a long trek it is therefore a good idea to bring along extra batteries. Because alkalines tend to drain more quickly in electronics, I would recommend using either NiMH or lithium batteries.

The Delorme PN-40 is a very nice GPS for consumer use. It is accurate, it holds its signal well, has a great display and comes with Topo which combined all make this unit hard to pass up. It's not perfect by any means, but it is still excellent and should be considered when looking for a good handheld GPS.
text_fidelity_b: DeLorme Earthmate PN-40 Waterproof Hiking GPS

text_fidelity_a:
Luoran MP3 Player with Bluetooth & WiFi, 4.0" IPS Display MP4 Portable Music Player with Full Touchscreen & Speaker, Metal Frame & Glass Back, Audiobook, Browser, Up to 512GB (Black) UPDATE 1/2/22:
I CANNOT RECOMMEND THIS PLAYER. My kid changed the password on the lock screen and then immediately forgot what it is, locking everyone out of the player. No big deal, right? Just hard reset the whole device and start over... except that there is NO WAY TO PERFORM A HARD RESET. You must be logged in and have access to the settings screen to reach the reset settings, if you are locked out you have exactly ZERO options.
I reached out to support, and they offered to send me files to flash and reset the device, but then realized there is no way to get into the bootloader for me. Rather than offer a replacement, they offered 40% off purchasing another. No thank you, that's a terrible design flaw. Avoid this product.

Original review:
This is a cute little media player that is clearly powered by Android under the hood. It is NOT a phone or tablet, it does NOT have the Play store... it is very much designed to be strictly a media player. However unlike other cheap mp3 devices which struggle to make their own UI, these guys took the short cut and decided not to re-invent the wheel, rather opting to use the open-source and readily available Android operating system to handle the interface. And let me tell you, that makes it GREAT!
No more struggling to find an archaic avi codec to make videos work like other players, no more learning how to navigate a backwards menu system, or finding out that certain bluetooth devices or wifi networks are incompatible... no, this has all the support that the Android platform does, and it does it smoothly and quite well! It even has one of my favorite mp3 playing apps, AIMP preinstalled! Nice!
If you wanted to use this for more than just the included functionality, you CAN side-load Android APK files to install new applications. I did that to put a few cute games on it, but major apps that are closely tied to Google services such as Youtube and Gmail will not work. But that shouldn't be expected, this is a media player after all that happens to run a popular OS under the hood. I really like it, and most importantly, so do my kids who I got it for!
text_fidelity_b: Luoran MP3 Player with Bluetooth & WiFi, 4.0" IPS Display MP4 Portable Music Player with Full Touchscreen & Speaker, Metal Frame & Glass Back, Audiobook, Browser, Up to 512GB (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White I ordered a three pack because I wanted one for my music room, living room and one for my girlfriend. Set up was super simple for the basics - connecting to a bluetooth speaker, your calendar (I use google's calendar), and a music source. For the latter I use Pandora and that, too, was simple.

The subtracted star is because while I own a few thousand dollars worth of MP3 albums that I purchased from Amazon, I cannot access them. Apparently you can only stream music from Amazon's cloud if you have Prime, and even then I am not sure that you can access any of your own music that resides in their cloud. To me that is a fail, and an indication that the business and requirements analysts who assisted in the development of this device do not fully understand customer requirements at a very basic level. Another nit is the iHeart Radio music source that is plain confusing to use.

Some other areas where this would be a LOT more useful is to have the ability to set up more than one route for traffic (currently I can only identify a single route, home-to-work or back, whereas I am frequently traveling from one place to the other and traffic conditions for those trips would be very helpful. The same for the calendar: you can get all events for a single day, but not for a week, or weekend so you still have to fire up a calendar app on your phone, tablet or computer if you want to get a sense of how busy you will be over a period longer than a day.

Still, for fifty bucks each - plus the discount for purchasing a three pack - this is a decent device that has proven to be surprisingly useful in my home. My girlfriend instantly took to hers too. In the week or so that I have been using it I find that I am growing increasingly dependent on mine for streaming music from Pandora, looking up quick information while I am reading or watching a documentary, and letting me know what is on my calendar for a specific day.

I have one of mine connected via bluetooth to a [[ASIN:B019PGACR0 LD Systems MAUI 5 Channel PA System]], and my girlfriend has hers connected to a [[ASIN:B00W8O6MJO Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker]], both of which greatly out perform the larger Echo. However I also use my other Dot with just its integrated speaker and it is more than adequate, even for streaming music since I have it on an end table.

Overall, for the current fifty bucks this is a bargain (warts notwithstanding), and while I purchased mine more out of curiosity all three have proven to be useful and practical.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic BEBP-115 15.6-Inch Laptop and Tablet Backpack, Black First a caveat: I am not of the generation who grew up carrying backpacks to school and I do not have a lot of shoulder/upper arm strength; in addition I have arthritis in my neck, so to me any backpack seems a bit strange, stiff, and awkward. Frankly, I think if I'd had to carry around all the books I did in junior high school in a backpack (none of my classes were near my homeroom locker, so there was none of this dropping books off routine--we only had three minutes to get between classes), I'd have severe back problems right now, remembering the thick English, math, science, Italian, and history textbooks, plus a full size ring binder. Oy.

Now to our backpack: I like this. We have less expensive backpacks in our home, to use as a "bug out" bag in case of emergency. This is much nicer: padding, quality of material, and lots of nice pockets (I am a pockets-type person). I particularly like the "hidden pocket" that faces your back, which would be useful for money or any other valuables if you were backpacking or traveling. I have preliminarily tested this by putting my laptop and my 10-inch tablet in the space provided and walking around for a bit. My laptop is six years old and weighs a ton. However, the padded shoulder straps and the sternum strap were helpful in keeping this balanced well on my back. I went up and down stairs a few times and did not feel unbalanced or "top heavy." (I do now, however, understand why people like Airbooks.)

In addition to the laptop pocket with the inner sleeve for the tablet, this has a central compartment with two pockets, one zipped, and an outside compartment with all sorts of slots for pens, memory cards, CDs, whatever. A small pocket on the top of the back could hold a cell phone or perhaps your printout of a boarding pass, parking ticket receipt, whatever, and there are two small pockets, one on each side, one with an opening so you could put an .mp3 player in the pocket and have your earbuds come out through it. This is all in addition to the "hidden pocket." There is a strong handle at either end of the backpack as well as a handle.

My goal is to give this a better workout at Dragoncon, where I can carry lunch and snacks and juice boxes in the central compartment, carry my tablet in the laptop compartment, and also carry my camera, instead of slinging a lunchbox and my camera case over my shoulder. It seems like a much better option. I also see it being useful on the occasional weekend trip. If it works out for me, it's possible my husband might enjoy one as well.

[September: This was really, really good at Dragoncon; I will be using a backpack again next year. Much better than carrying the lunchbox and the camera separately and wearing a pouch. I put my tablet in the laptop pocket, my lunch things (juice boxes, sandwiches, snacks, fruit) in the middle pocket, and the camera in the outermost pocket. The little pocket at the top held my spare cell phone batteries, and my wallet was in the hidden pocket. This backpack needs a strap at the bottom, and, instead of an iPod holder, a water bottle holder. That's the only thing I can see wrong with it. Yeah, I could have put a water bottle inside with my lunch.]

[PS I liked this so much I bought my husband one for Christmas.]
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic BEBP-115 15.6-Inch Laptop and Tablet Backpack, Black

The biggest problem my mother had was adjusting to the wide-screen 16:9 format of the Fire tablet compared to the old fashioned 4:3 format of her old tablet. This also had a faster processor with two more cores and four more megs of ram augmented by an 8gb memory card to expand storage. The blue color is quite attractive. The tablet so far runs everything she wants and I've even taught her to use the appstore to download her favorite games. The colors are sharp and clear. Video is smooth and while we watched only one half hour show so far there was no pausing or buffering.
I think the only thing I honestly dislike and it's my fault for not seeing it when this was a Prime Day special. I can forgive the tablet going out of stock and not being alerted to that fact when we placed the order. What I find somewhat insulting is this is the ONLY Fire tabled that comes with a limited 90 day warranty while every other Fire tablet has a minimum of one year warranty. I think there's something wrong with that. I probably would have bought this anyhow. My mom can't stand the weight of my 10" tablet (an ounce heavier than the 10" Fire) and the 8" was (and still is) available in one configuration (color, memory, special offers, etc.) which wasn't attractive and appeared to be fairly heavy.
So far so good. The tablet is functioning properly with a couple glitches here and there but every touch screen tablet and computer has similar issues. Other than what should have been a year warranty like every other Fire, Kindle, TV stick/device and Echo/tap has. That's just wrong and unfair to people buying a specific size of tablet.

text_fidelity_a: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White We have all three of the Echo products: The Dot, The Tap, and the original Echo. The Dot works very similarly to the original Echo. You say the wake word, you give a command or question, it responds. It does have a speaker itself, but it doesn't get as loud as the original Echo or the Tap. All of the devices will sync together in one Amazon app, but they all still work independently. Meaning, if I set an alarm on the Dot, only the alarm on the Dot goes off. But with the app on my phone, I can access all the devices in the one place. The Original Echo is better for larger areas. the Dot is ideal if you already have a sound system you would like to connect the Dot to, or small spaces like bathrooms or bedrooms. The Dot is great for kids. My daughter has it in her room so she can ask it how to spell words and such. The Tap is an entirely different beast, in my opinion. No wake word. Touch and talk. But it works via Bluetooth and wifi for on the go use using your cellular device. The Echo Dot does not come with a remote. Like the Original Echo, it needs to be plugged into the wall and needs wifi. (The Tap has a chargeable battery.) They are all great devices, though Amazon still has some work to be done on them. Each has a different place where it is the ideal choice, so which you should choose really depends on your needs.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

Logitech NEW Logitech Webcam C210 (Cameras & Frames) I received the Logitech VideoCam and was surprised at one, how easy and quick the setup took; second, I was amazed at the quality of the picture. This is my first time at WebCam and was apprehensive at the standard of quality. But in 1,2,3 steps it was up. The voices are clear and it depends whether you use Logitech viewing or Skype, but Logitech has a more refined lip movement to voice coordination. Again...this is a perfect picture!

Surprisingly, the 3MP photo option is quite impressive. I love the shoot picture instantly. You can quickly add a friend to chat with, just enter their email address. Either at your end of the recipients end you can quickly snap a picture and that pic can be the photo of choice for the friend or family. It is easy to have several different pictures on the interface of the Webcam; I dragged a few from the desktop. My webcam sits comfortably on top of the computer. If I need to remove the camera from the top of computer to show a different view of my background, or reveal other parts of the house, I can do that easily with the 5-feet long attached cord, although it could be longer.

You can make several adjustments, and the light adjustment is automatic, the mic is noise cancelling, however, I have not the need to test that yet.

What I like is that anytime someone on your contact list is at the computer, you can have a small message pop up that lets you know they are available. My two current contacts are using Windows XP; while I am on Windows Vista.

If you are someone you know is vascillating between getting a Webcam, I encourage them to do so, especially if they have family miles away like I do. Many people do not like to be on camera, and for me, I don't either because I have to look decent an any moment a call comes in. Try it.... You may like it! ....Rizzo
text_fidelity_b: Logitech NEW Logitech Webcam C210 (Cameras & Frames)

text_fidelity_a:
LotFancy 7 Inch 16:9 TFT Color LCD Widescreen Car Rear View Monitor Bundle with Remote and Waterproof Camera Many cars on the market come with a rear-view camera that allows for seeing where the vehicle is moving when in reverse. Often the view appears on a dashboard screen. This is handy when parking and maneuvering while the vehicle is backing up. For vehicles that do not have a rear-view camera the alternative is to add on a kit that provides the same functionality. This is my first experience with such a kit and so far I am pleased with it. It does require doing a little work on the vehicle to set it up but the effort is worth it.

The package contains everything needed to set up this camera system. In addition to the camera and the screen, the kit includes the mounting screws for the actual camera as well as all of the wiring to connect everything together and to the power (reverse lights). There is also a mini-remote for interacting with the video screen though this is slightly inconvenient.

I spent a good deal of time reading and rereading the directions and concluded that the instructions could have been better. There are three pieces of documentation in the box; one shows a generalized set of four different configurations for connecting everything together (the fourth diagram on this sheet matches the configuration you want), one is a photocopied image of a wired system and the third is a “User’s Manual” which is one half-sheet of paper with a brief summarization of the product. There really needs to be a better documentation set than this.

If you are not skilled in working with electrical systems, either plan on this taking a good while or have someone you trust install the system. It’s not especially hard to set one of these up, but it does take some patience and a little bit of knowledge of the layout of the car’s wiring. I have worked on car electrical systems in the distant past so I had a vague familiarity, but it still took me a while to have everything set up and working.

Once wired the system is fairly straightforward to use. If it is wired up properly (meaning everything is connected to power on both ends and the two main components can see one another) it works nicely. The image when the camera is feeding to the monitor is bright and reasonably clear; the brightness can be adjusted as needed which helps when using this system at night. Another reviewer commented that he used a different camera connected to this system - while I am personally satisfied with the image quality, it’s reassuring to know that you can use another video camera if desired or necessary.

The addition of the remote will appeal to some, but for me it’s a component that can easily be lost. The menu system on the monitor provides the same functionality as the remote and this is good enough for me.

This is my first experience with rear-view video systems and though it gave me a little trouble setting up it was from lack of good documentation and inexperience, not from being a bad product. Once installed this is a nice and easy-to-use video system. Time will tell how long it works.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy 7 Inch 16:9 TFT Color LCD Widescreen Car Rear View Monitor Bundle with Remote and Waterproof Camera

text_fidelity_a:
CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance [[VIDEOID:5b880a1d8f11ab783ee7340a330164be]] I ordered the ‘CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance’ for review and would like to share my thoughts.

I will lay this out as pros and cons and give some final thoughts.

Pros: The kit as a whole is well made.
Cameras are well made.
The 4tb hard drive is a good name brand and seems to be performing quite well.
The video quality is good.
The kit comes with 8X good quality 50 foot CAT5 cables (more on this in the cons)

Cons: The included cables are only 50 feet each. In a home install, if you are trying to run cameras to all corners of your house, 50 feet is not long enough in my case. I only used three of these cables. I had to buy more cable (CAT6) for the longer runs.
Although the cameras are well made, because they are of the Dome type, if you adjust the cameras to point at much of an angle, you run into issues at night when the IR lights turn on. This causes the IR lights to reflect back at the cameras (See attached video) The best angle for the cameras are to point straight down or at a very slight angle.
Speaking of angles, these cameras only have a 90 degree diagonal viewing angle which was a little disappointing.
When viewing the live feed, sometimes the video feed gets distorted for a couple of seconds.
The software of the NVR is a little overwhelming and hard to navigate. This is probably due to the fact that I have never used this type of system before. There are a lot of options in the Software which does not work with these specific cameras, such as Human Detection or PTZ (Pan Tilt Zoom). Not having the PTZ is really no big deal but it would have been nice to have the Human Detection so that the cameras don’t alarm when the wind blows the trees and shrubs.
There is an option to send an email when there is motion detected on the cameras but I was never able to get that to work.
Although there is an email option, I would have liked to see a text option.

Overall I am actually happy with this kit. It at least provides peace-of-mind knowing that the cameras are always recording and with the included 4tb hard drive in this kit, it provides many hours of footage. I hope that this was somewhat helpful.
text_fidelity_b: CTVISION 4K 8MP Home Business Wired Security Camera Systems,8-Channel 4K 8MP PoE Network Video Recorder(4TB HDD),8pc 4K (4X1080P) Outdoor Dome PoE IP Camera,Free App,P2P Cloud,Onvif,Video Surveillance

iCrius Reading Light for Bed, Table Lamps for Bedroom, Dimmable LED Desk Lamp I received this as a free review sample. It is close to being perfect, but there is one thing that prevented me from awarding it five stars: the power cable is hardwired into the lamp. It's basically a standard USB cable that should have been a standard USB micro or USB C style, but is instead unremovable from the lamp. That means that if you damage the cable instead of replacing it with a readily available USB cable the repair cost is probably greater than replacing the entire lamp - unless you are handy at such things.

Aside from the cable, I love this lamp. For one thing the clamp will firmly hold the entire lamp in place on a music stand's thin, metal shelf. Plus the gooseneck, while flexible,holds the lamp where you place it. I have similar lamp that will move position if you bump it, so for me this one is vastly better than most.

I do love the fact that I can power this from a wall using the included charging adapter or from a battery such as a [[ASIN:B014O2AXB0 Kikicom Power Bank]] (or similar model). Also you can actually power it from a laptop's USB port, which makes it perfect for small study desks. The included charger has a 1 Amp port for powering the lamp and a port marked 2.1 Amps for charging phones and tablets. To be honest, the 2.1 port is not especially fast and I suspect outputs less than the labeled capacity, but it still can keep up with my tablet.

Bottom line: if you area musician this is possibly the best music stand lamp in its price range (and it is not described as a music stand lamp!) For reading and even small room lighting it is also excellent. It would be an easy five stars had the cable been standard.
text_fidelity_b: iCrius Reading Light for Bed, Table Lamps for Bedroom, Dimmable LED Desk Lamp

It comes with a little stand to make it a table light, a wrist holder to make it a jogging light, and a magnetic holder to make it a strip light wherever you might need some extra illumination. An on/off switch along with a dimmer knob would have been the more traditional approach but that would have clashed with the sleek styling. So I can live with the finger tapping method. I'm still not sure I have the wrist strap set correctly but since I don't jog it's not a big deal to me. The other minor flaw is that the usb recharging cord has a different plug in than the other rechargeable devices I have. That means one more cord to keep track of but again that's not a big deal. Just looking at this thing makes me smile. That and its versatility far outweigh the minor negatives mentioned here so I happily give it five stars.

text_fidelity_a: Western Digital 4TB WD Blue PC Internal Hard Drive HDD - 5400 RPM, SATA 6 Gb/s, 256 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD40EZAZ The price of these is usually low enough to consider buying them new for off-line storage. Something most people don't consider using a hard drive for. 4TB has become small for my purposes, but as off-line storage I don't want to risk more than that on one drive. It's much simpler to archive data on a 4TB hard drive in a dock and keep it in a case than to burn 4TB to a stack of Blu-Ray disks every few months, and DVDs are completely out of the question. I'm archiving around 20TB of 4K video that I've captured with GoPros so far. Most of it is on "retired" drives, but I've run out of reliable older drives and I think I'll be upgrading to these in the future. They're unlikely to store data forever without some degradation, but rewriting the data once a year won't wear them out for decades. These will not work well in an NAS or even a RAID array in a PC, and shouldn't be used in a PC with more than one or two hard drives anyway. They're not designed to cope with vibration from several other drives, but as a single drive or for data backup they're fine. It's a capable drive for typical home use. For full-time use in an array, the Red Plus and Red Pro drives are what I get. If you need to store large amounts of data off-line, or if you just need a new drive in a home PC, this is a good choice.
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 4TB WD Blue PC Internal Hard Drive HDD - 5400 RPM, SATA 6 Gb/s, 256 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD40EZAZ
